ns2:group.ns2:title: Schools are catching onto tech’s playbook
ns2:group.ns2:description:
For years, big tech companies have embedded their products into the classroom whether through Google's Chromebooks or computer science curricula developed by Apple or Microsoft. The industry pushed a generation of kids to foster coding skills with the promise of high-paying jobs. Now, those students are finding themselves less in demand as AI takes over, and the industry seems to be repeating its playbook. Senior policy reporter Lauren Feiner talks to Natasha Singer, author of the new book "Coding Kids," about how big tech worked its way into the classroom, and why Natasha is optimistic about educators’ response to the AI push.

The Verge’s editor-in-chief Nilay Patel takes a closer look at the foldable, which has a 5.4-inch display but opens to a 7.6-inch panel. Apple went with a matte finish with the Duo’s inner screen which helps with glare, but also helps mask the crease. The Duo starts at $1,999, with preorders beginning October 16th and sales starting October 23rd. Was it worth the wait?
